transcript: So The Sound of music is coming back to Broadway, and I think it is fair to wonder if this is going to have, like, an actually lavish set or if it's gonna feel kind of barebones and sparse in the staging the way that ragtime did. But I think it's a little too early to say, and I am gonna defend Lear DeBessonet a little bit from the accusations that she only does, like, concert style staging. I think it's important to consider that before Lear DeBessonet was at Lincoln Centre, she was at encores, and before that, she was at PublicWorks. PublicWorks, for those who don't know, is a subsidiary of the Public Theatre, which is basically a hybrid of professional and community theatre. So she went from that to doing staged concerts at encores, three of which transferred to Broadway. So between that and her production of Hercules from PublicWorks, it feels like all of her, like, Broadway musical style work so far, all of her, like, most highly publicized work, has been created for a very, very specific context and then just kind of unceremoniously transplanted into a different context. And I guess the counter argument is, like, when these productions transplanted to a different setting, I guess Lear DeBessonet had the opportunity to beef up the staging and make it feel more like a fully staged production, and she didn’t. But then, like, I don't know, it wouldn't be a transfer Like, maybe the only reason that these productions got the money to transfer was because it was so cheap to produce. And, like, That’s not really her fault. Like, she has done other work outside of these organizations before. We actually haven't seen her build a Broadway musical production from scratch that was, like, originally intended for Broadway. Not to mention with the shadow of Bartlett's Asher’s previous Rogers and Hammerstein revivals at Lincoln Center looming over her. Like, I don't know, maybe it will end up being kind of sparsely designed, but still, I just would say at this point, it's too early to assume that just because of her work that she created specifically for encores and publicworks.
